claims.text: The Court held the advice to prorogue Parliament unlawful and the resulting prorogation null and without effect.
claims.locator: [2019] UKSC 41, paragraphs 50, 61 and 69–70
claims.verification_note: Checked the Court’s own conclusion and remedy, paragraphs 61 and 69–70, rather than allegations in the procedural history. No criminality or inferred motive is admitted.

claims.text: The Committee concluded that Johnson deliberately misled the House. The summary records its reasoning, his denials and his response to provisional conclusions.
claims.locator: Summary, paragraphs 11–17
claims.verification_note: The summary supports the attributed Committee conclusion. June 2023 committee conduct is outside the premiership. Full representations and Commons disposition remain outside this bounded verification.

claims.text: The committees identified both vaccination successes and serious weaknesses in the early pandemic response, including delayed lockdown and shortcomings affecting vulnerable groups.
claims.locator: Opening summary and principal findings
claims.verification_note: Both strengths and weaknesses are present in the official inquiry announcement. This verifies the summary, not all claims in the full report or personal prime ministerial responsibility.

claims.text: The government recorded Johnson’s Kyiv visit and announced additional military assistance and World Bank lending guarantees.
claims.locator: Paragraphs describing assistance and lending guarantees
claims.verification_note: The announcement records military aid and guarantees. Delivery and effect have not been independently established by this release.

claims.text: The announcement sets out monthly publication of ministerial gifts and hospitality, including values, and an independent adviser’s power to initiate investigations without a prime ministerial veto.
claims.locator: Gifts and hospitality rules; independent adviser powers
claims.verification_note: The dated announcement supports monthly disclosure and the no-veto investigation provision. Enforcement and actual compliance remain unverified.

claims.text: The register includes Arsenal tickets and hospitality received on 17 August 2024 and declared on 10 September 2024. Other entries concern earlier dates or periods straddling the start of the premiership.
claims.locator: Category 3; Arsenal entry received 17 August 2024; accommodation entry 29 May–13 July 2024
claims.verification_note: The Arsenal entry confirms receipt/acceptance on 17 August and registration on 10 September. Other benefits predate office or straddle it; no breach finding is inferred.

claims.text: Starmer condemned violent disorder, referred to targeted Muslim and other minority communities, and stated that the government would support the police and pursue criminal enforcement.
claims.locator: Speech transcript, paragraphs on targeted communities and policing
claims.verification_note: The transcript supports the limited description of words delivered. Operational outcomes and effects on communities remain outside this source’s proof.

claims.text: The Treasury announced expanded Winter Fuel Payment eligibility in England and Wales using a £35,000 income threshold, following the narrower arrangements introduced for winter 2024/25.
claims.locator: Eligibility announcement and Further background
claims.verification_note: Treasury announcement confirms the threshold and the narrower 2024/25 background. Attribution to Starmer’s personal reasoning remains unsupported.

claims.text: The inspection identified serious weaknesses in victim service, crime recording, investigation and governance, while recognising some improvements and a programme of change.
claims.locator: Printed pages 8–12: summary, supervision and governance, causes of concern; inspection conducted September–October 2020
claims.verification_note: The report confirms the September–October 2020 inspection and adverse as well as qualifying findings. Footer confirms December 2020, but an exact publication day is not established.

claims.text: The police force announced removal from enhanced monitoring and described improvements in call handling, recording and investigation.
claims.locator: Opening announcement and crime-recording/investigation passages
claims.verification_note: The institutional account is now corroborated on the narrow removal-from-monitoring decision by the inspector’s original letter V05. Other performance figures and personal credit remain separately unverified.

claims.text: GAO identified inadequate CMS planning and oversight, increased contract costs and delayed functionality. The record includes agency responses and later implementation of recommendations.
claims.locator: What GAO Found; Recommendations for Executive Action
claims.verification_note: GAO highlights confirm planning and oversight weaknesses, cost increases and delayed functionality. Dynamic follow-up records implemented recommendations; that is separate from the 2014 original finding.

claims.text: The Board recommended ending bulk telephone-record collection, citing legal, privacy and effectiveness concerns. The report includes separate statements by two members.
claims.locator: Printed page 16, Recommendation 1; introduction and annex contents
claims.verification_note: Recommendation 1 supports the attributed legal/privacy/value concerns; contents identify separate member statements. They must be read before treating the conclusions as unanimous. This is not a judicial criminal finding.

claims.text: Obama set out announced intelligence reforms and further privacy work, presenting the need to balance security and civil liberties.
claims.locator: Speech, reform proposals and closing discussion of privacy review
claims.verification_note: Reform announcements and privacy work are in the 17 January speech. The speech predates the 23 January PCLOB report and is not described as a response to it.

claims.text: At the Newtown vigil Obama acknowledged bereaved families, praised responders and community support, and committed to work on preventing further shootings.
claims.locator: Speech at Newtown High School, passages on families and prevention
claims.verification_note: Transcript confirms the limited account of acknowledgement, praise and commitments. Empathy over the whole term and prevention outcomes are not established.

claims.text: The catalogue identifies the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as Public Law 111–148, dated 23 March 2010.
claims.locator: Content Details
claims.verification_note: GovInfo catalogue confirms law identifier and 23 March 2010 date. No substantive statutory or implementation conclusion is inferred from metadata.

claims.text: The analysis reports changes in health insurance coverage and other indicators, and warns that numerical changes do not determine presidential credit or blame.
claims.locator: Analysis introduction and Health Insurance section
claims.verification_note: The analysis discusses insurance indicators and explicitly cautions against automatic presidential credit/blame. Original datasets and causal attribution remain outstanding.

claims.text: The official record documents the handover from Scholz to Merz on 6 May 2025 and includes their statements.
claims.locator: Dated introduction and handover statements
claims.verification_note: Dated handover record supports 6 May 2025 and observable transfer conduct. Ceremonial statements do not establish consistent humility.

claims.text: Scholz announced a security-policy shift following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, including a defence fund, commitments to allies and measures on energy security and household pressures.
claims.locator: Fourth policy area: defence capability; energy security and relief package
claims.verification_note: Official English text supports the announced defence fund, allied commitments and energy/household measures. Delivery is not established. German wording still requires review for any contested phrase.

claims.text: The independent review records that Burnham commissioned it and prioritised the experiences of bereaved families and other affected people.
claims.locator: Sections 1.2–1.3, printed pages 11–12
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: The report records some respondents’ positive accounts of personal visits by the mayor and chief constable.
claims.locator: Section 2.22, printed pages 49–50
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: The report also records that some respondents outside Manchester felt overlooked or less well supported. This is not a finding of Burnham’s sole responsibility.
claims.locator: Section 2.23, printed page 50
claims.verification_note: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

claims.text: GMCA records Burnham’s decision to introduce bus franchising in March 2021, with the first services running in September 2023 and final rollout in January 2025.
claims.locator: The journey to franchised bus services
claims.verification_note: Official overview now retrieved. It records the March 2021 decision and rollout dates. Its budget, patronage and comparative claims are not independently validated here.

claims.text: The Court’s press release states that the Second Supplementary Budget Act 2021 was incompatible with specified Basic Law provisions and void; the operative judgement confirms this.
claims.locator: Press release opening; V06 operative judgement
claims.verification_note: Previously inaccessible press release now retrieved. Its operative account agrees with the separately retrieved judgement V06. Invalid legislation is not a finding of personal dishonesty.

claims.text: Johnson apologised, acknowledged public sacrifices and said he had believed the May 2020 garden gathering was a work event; he accepted that he should have acted differently.
claims.locator: Opening answer and later work-event answers
claims.limitations: The apology and explanation are recorded words, not proof that the explanation was correct; compare the privileges findings about in-period statements.

claims.text: Geidt criticised incomplete disclosure of messages relevant to the flat-refurbishment investigation and insufficient regard for his role; he distinguished that criticism from his earlier interests assessment.
claims.locator: Disclosure, notification and annex discussion
claims.limitations: Preserve the qualified finding rather than alleging that a bribe or personal corruption was proved. Publication is later than the letter date.

claims.text: Johnson thanked staff and the public, referred critically to the circumstances of succession and pledged support for Liz Truss and the new government.
claims.locator: Final speech, succession and closing paragraphs
claims.limitations: Mixed observable communication; do not infer his private motives or validate achievement claims in the speech.

claims.text: Johnson set out governing commitments in his first Downing Street speech.
claims.locator: Opening governing programme and commitments
claims.limitations: A baseline for comparing promises with later decisions, not delivery evidence or proof of public-service motivation.

claims.text: The full report sets out its finding about misleading the House, Johnson’s account and arguments, and its reasons for rejecting aspects of them.
claims.locator: Conclusions and sections on what Johnson told the House; representations considered in report
claims.limitations: Later committee conduct and sanctions must not be scored as premiership behaviour. Only relevant sections were reviewed, not every evidential attachment.

claims.text: Geidt raised the question of the Ministerial Code’s legal-compliance duty following the Prime Minister’s fixed penalty notice and called for a public explanation of the Prime Minister’s position.
claims.locator: Preface: fixed penalty notice and public confidence in the Code
claims.limitations: A question and advice are not a concluded independent finding that the Code was breached. Original publication day is not established in this packet.

claims.text: ITV reported Downing Street’s statement that Starmer had paid for gifts and hospitality and commissioned revised principles.
claims.locator: Report and quoted Downing Street statement
claims.limitations: A reported official account, not audited banking evidence. Repayment does not erase acceptance or establish that every conflict was resolved.

claims.text: Starmer used the phrase island of strangers in explaining his government’s immigration proposals.
claims.locator: Transcript paragraph containing island of strangers
claims.limitations: Assess treatment of people and communication, not agreement with immigration restrictions. Later regret is a separate event.

claims.text: The report quotes Starmer’s regret and explanation in his Observer interview.
claims.locator: Reported interview quotations
claims.limitations: One interview origin, not independent corroboration merely because it is syndicated. The original interview has now been retrieved as NKS09.

claims.text: Starmer announced his resignation, thanked staff and the public, credited collective work and pledged support for his successor.
claims.locator: Resignation, successor and concluding thanks
claims.limitations: Verifies words and announced transfer, not the speech’s claims about the economy, public services or other achievements.

claims.text: Starmer presented service and public trust as governing commitments in his first speech.
claims.locator: Initial governing commitments
claims.limitations: Rhetorical baseline only; subsequent behaviour and institutional decisions must supply the assessment.

claims.text: GMCA states that Burnham launched a homelessness fund as a first mayoral act and donated part of his salary.
claims.locator: Opening paragraphs on fund and salary; displayed publication timestamp
claims.limitations: Page timestamp is 13 December 2018, while the account describes the start of the mayoralty. Event timing is contextualised by NAB07. Do not call this an audited recurring donation record or assume the 2020 goal was met.

claims.text: Burnham’s statement acknowledged unacceptable lack of progress, said the report was accepted and victims apologised to, and announced changes in force leadership.
claims.locator: Mayor’s statement on report acceptance, apology and leadership
claims.limitations: Direct record of acknowledgement and announced action. It does not by itself establish adequate prior oversight or completed reform.

claims.text: The meeting record states that Burnham registered an interest concerning LEVI funding under the capital-funding item.
claims.locator: Decision under Declarations of Interest, Item 3
claims.limitations: A narrow instance of disclosure. Do not infer a personal financial conflict, recusal or consistent compliance from it; publication date is not stated.

claims.text: The statement accepted serious inspection issues and announced measures including a dedicated route for victims whose crimes were not recorded or appropriately handled.
claims.locator: Report response and victim hotline paragraphs
claims.limitations: Announced steps require follow-up. Distinguish the force-data reference period from the later inspection dates and the mayor’s own responsibilities.

claims.text: Obama accepted responsibility for counterterrorism operations, apologised to the families and described review of the operation that killed the hostages.
claims.locator: Statement paragraphs on responsibility, apology and review
claims.limitations: An acknowledgement of grave harm is relevant; it does not erase harm, prove the adequacy of safeguards or establish full accountability for every operation.

claims.text: Obama accepted responsibility for the health-law rollout, acknowledged loss of credibility and discussed corrective action.
claims.locator: DCPD-201300781, printed page 4 and subsequent health-marketplace answers
claims.limitations: Read alongside GAO’s independent findings and later follow-up; statements about repair are not evidence that every defect was resolved.

claims.text: Obama congratulated the president-elect and instructed his team to work towards a successful peaceful transition.
claims.locator: Reproduced speech paragraphs on call, team instructions and transition
claims.limitations: Observable communication and instruction, not confirmation of every transition action or acceptance of every substantive policy of the successor.

claims.text: The order requires an ethics pledge for appointees and contains restrictions, administration provisions and a written-waiver mechanism.
claims.locator: Pledge, section 3 Waiver and administration provisions
claims.limitations: Instituted rules do not establish personal sacrifice, universal compliance or improper use of waivers. The waiver mechanism must not be omitted from a favourable account.

claims.text: Scholz accepted the constitutional court decision as politically binding, described adjustments and framed the implications in terms of crisis management.
claims.locator: Opening court-response passages
claims.limitations: English summaries are research paraphrases of German. Acceptance is observable; the speech does not undo invalid budgeting or independently establish programme effectiveness.

claims.text: Scholz announced the finance minister’s dismissal, attributed serious failings to Lindner and proposed a confidence vote to enable an election.
claims.locator: Reasons for dismissal and intended confidence timetable
claims.limitations: Allegations about Lindner are Scholz’s position, not established facts here. Coalition and constitutional constraints matter; neither dismissal nor remaining in office proves ambition over service.

claims.text: The Bundestag records Scholz’s Article 68 confidence motion and its defeat on 16 December 2024.
claims.locator: Motion, vote result and constitutional procedure
claims.limitations: The outcome is not a popularity or leadership-quality measure; relevance lies in use of the constitutional procedure.

claims.text: The report records Scholz accepting responsibility for his party’s result and saying he would carry out his duties until the last day.
claims.locator: Scholz response to early election results
claims.limitations: The election outcome itself is excluded from scoring. An attributed acceptance is not independent proof of broad self-correction.

claims.text: The analysis notes that the budget statement did not include an apology and criticises its lack of a concrete timetable.
claims.locator: Sections on timetable and Keine Entschuldigung
claims.limitations: Labelled analytical interpretation, not a new legal finding or proof of personality. Use with the original speech NOS01.

claims.text: Johnson apologised for the adviser’s position and incomplete explanation, defended parts of his office’s handling and proposed more support and information access for the adviser.
claims.locator: Letter paragraphs on apology, disclosure and proposed steps
claims.limitations: Direct acknowledgement and promises; implementation is not established. Read alongside Geidt rather than treating the response as an exoneration.

claims.text: The Plan sets out named milestones and numerical targets and presents them as a basis for public accountability.
claims.locator: Foreword and milestone list, printed pages 5–7; chapter headings
claims.limitations: Relevant sections of the 48-page PDF reviewed. Targets and institutional reform intentions are not achieved outcomes; no full-document implementation audit claimed.

claims.text: The report quotes Burnham’s letter apologising for historical discrimination, his statement about operational independence and Tatchell’s view that a mayoral apology did not replace a force apology.
claims.locator: Quoted letter and recipient response
claims.limitations: Original letter not retrieved here. The mayor’s 2025 acknowledgement is in period; the historical abuses described are not attributed to his own mayoralty.

claims.text: The study describes citizen participation in the Foreign Office’s strategy process and argues that control techniques limited its opening.
claims.locator: German and English abstracts
claims.limitations: The study concerns a Foreign Office process, not a finding of Scholz’s individual empathy or manipulation. Issue year is 2025; online publication is 20 June 2024.

claims.text: DWP reports recipients under changed eligibility and explains comparisons with earlier winters.
claims.locator: Main stories and eligibility/comparability notes
claims.limitations: Retrospective source about an in-period winter. Counts, recipients and beneficiaries differ; this is context, not proof of Starmer’s personal listening or a moral score.

claims.text: The interview reports Burnham’s salary pledge and questions him about homelessness, mental health and how support would work.
claims.locator: Introduction and interview questions on the homelessness fund
claims.limitations: Directly questioned commitments, not bank records or measured results; charity-focused publication has an explicit public-interest perspective.

claims.text: The strategy connects national-security and international-policy objectives to priority actions to 2025 in a strategic framework.
claims.locator: Introduction and Strategic Framework
claims.limitations: Accessible text updated 2 July 2021; original publication day not established by this file alone. This establishes an articulated strategy, not coherent delivery across all policy.

claims.text: In the original interview Starmer regretted the phrase, said he had not intended the historical echo and acknowledged that he should have scrutinised the speech more carefully.
claims.locator: Interview passage discussing the May immigration speech
claims.limitations: Original published interview, not unedited recording. It establishes an attributed acknowledgement and explanation, not that the explanation is independently proved.

claims.text: Rachel Brand’s separate statement disagrees with ending the telephone-record programme without an adequate alternative and supports many other recommendations.
claims.locator: Annex A, printed pages 208–213
claims.limitations: Dissent is not an exoneration. Preserve majority and separate reasoning without counting members as source votes.

claims.text: Elisebeth Collins Cook’s separate statement supports modifications but disputes the report’s statutory-authorisation, constitutional and efficacy analyses.
claims.locator: Annex B, printed pages 214–218
claims.limitations: Dissent is not an exoneration. Preserve majority and separate reasoning without counting members as source votes.

claims.text: In his 17 December 2021 letter, Geidt maintained the fundamental assessment that the payment did not create a conflict or reasonably perceived conflict, while qualifying other conclusions and criticising disclosure.
claims.locator: Letter opening: impact on earlier advice; subsequent disclosure sections
claims.limitations: A specific finding about the interests created by this payment, not general exoneration of all conduct or a finding that the investigation received full disclosure.

claims.text: Johnson instructed people to stay at home, explained permitted exceptions and announced that restrictions would be reviewed in three weeks against evidence.
claims.locator: Stay-at-home instructions, exceptions and three-week review paragraphs
claims.limitations: Text establishes the content and clarity of communication, not inner composure, public compliance or whether the timing was appropriate.

claims.text: Johnson warned that more families would lose loved ones, described the scientific advice and set out the measures then being taken.
claims.locator: Opening risk warning and measures
claims.limitations: Compare with 23 March rather than treating a changed response as automatically inconsistent. Claims of scientific guidance remain the speaker’s account.

claims.text: The reproduced statement acknowledges grief and anger, calls for solidarity, provides emergency contact information and asks people to share trusted information.
claims.locator: Speech and emergency-information paragraphs
claims.limitations: Official page displays a later 2018 timestamp. GC_AB03 corroborates the 23 May 2017 occasion; no claim of contemporaneous website publication is made.

claims.text: In the reported interview Burnham said he would accept legally imposed restrictions while explaining concerns about harm to residents.
claims.locator: Quotation from interview with Kay Burley
claims.limitations: A reported interview, not an independently tested account of negotiations or proof that all his communication remained calm.

claims.text: Obama distinguished concern from panic, described consultation with public-health officials and explained why they did not recommend closing the Mexican border.
claims.locator: Press-conference question and answer reproduced in post
claims.limitations: Direct communication evidence; medical appropriateness and implementation require other records. Publication is a day after the conference.

claims.text: Obama advocated science-based monitoring, distinguished facts from fear and said he would obtain input from returning health workers.
claims.locator: Monitoring guidance and health-worker input paragraphs
claims.limitations: Announced consultation is not proof that it occurred; reassurance does not prove effectiveness or consistent composure across the presidency.

claims.text: The visually inspected cover identifies Obama’s personal incumbent financial disclosure for calendar year 2015 and includes signatures.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, visually inspected
claims.limitations: Text extraction is empty. Only the cover was inspected visually; no asset inventory, compliance conclusion or absence of conflicts is claimed.

claims.text: The White House announced the charities designated to receive the Nobel Prize proceeds.
claims.locator: Announcement and charity allocation list
claims.limitations: Announcement alone establishes intention. The subsequent transfer confirmation in GS_BO04 is the stronger action evidence.

claims.text: The account records citizens’ questions about social insurance, skills, families and refugee employment, with Scholz’s direct responses.
claims.locator: Topic-specific question-and-answer sections
claims.limitations: Government-selected account of a managed event, not an independent measure of empathy or proof that answers caused policy changes.

claims.text: The account records Scholz answering citizens about pensions and family support, including a commitment concerning basic support for children.
claims.locator: Pensions and family-support question-and-answer passages
claims.limitations: Verifies recorded personal engagement, not delivery of the commitment. Do not turn attendance or a promise into sustained responsiveness.

claims.text: Scholz acknowledged citizens’ anxiety, described allied coordination and sanctions, and said the conflict should be prevented from spreading to other European countries.
claims.locator: Opening acknowledgement and allied-coordination passages
claims.limitations: Content of an acute-crisis address, not proof of internal calm, military outcomes or the completeness of preparation.

claims.text: The archive lists declared functions and an interest in the law partnership Zimmermann, Scholz und Partner.
claims.locator: Veröffentlichungspflichtige Angaben; functions and participations
claims.limitations: Disclosure is not proof of an improper conflict or of its resolution. The archive does not establish the decision-level recusal and benefit history needed for Service.

claims.text: The charity’s accounts identify a £12,375 contribution from patron Andy Burnham in the period and a £15,125 comparative figure for 2023.
claims.locator: Accounts related-party note and fundraising section; PDF pages 11 and 41
claims.limitations: Recipient-filed accounts, not personal bank statements or a guarantee of all annual payments. Do not infer a universal salary percentage or equate contributions with overall public-duty quality.

claims.text: The annual report identifies £11,050 donated by Burnham and separately describes a £10,000 Sky speaker-fee contribution on his behalf in lieu of some direct payments.
claims.locator: Individual donations/fundraising section, PDF page 11
claims.limitations: Do not add the Sky fee as another direct personal payment or extrapolate a continuous payment history. The report explains an allocation spanning reporting periods.

claims.text: The tax-release explanation states that Obama directed the Nobel Prize funds to charities, with the prize excluded from income and no charitable deduction for its value.
claims.locator: Nobel Prize tax-treatment paragraphs
claims.limitations: An official tax explanation, not a new audit or proof of motive. The account should not imply an additional charitable deduction was claimed.

claims.text: Obama’s signed instruction directs the award to charities; the Foundation’s signed 12 April confirmation states that the proceeds were transferred on 18 March 2010.
claims.locator: PDF page 1 instruction; page 4 Foundation confirmation; visually inspected
claims.limitations: Four-page scan inspected visually; no automated OCR claim. It establishes this documented disposal of an award, not absence of other conflicts or a general judgement about motives.

claims.text: ITV’s dated coverage records Burnham’s address after the Arena attack and his expression of grief, shock and anger.
claims.locator: Dated update and quoted address
claims.limitations: Corroborates occasion and words; does not verify emotional state or the quality of emergency-service operations.
